newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais asked to delay rice planting as rains late.
newsitem.headline: Thais asked to delay rice planting as rains late.

text.p: Thai farmers in some areas of the country have been advised to delay rice planting because of a lack of much-needed rains, an agriculture ministry official said on Wednesday.
They said it was too early to say if the freak dry spell was due to the side effects of the El Nino weather phenomenon or if the country was facing a possible drought.
"Normally, farmers will grow rice after the Buddhist Lent on July 20 which is the usual time when rains start falling regularly," said one official.
"But up to now there has only been scattered rain here and there. Dry spells have been detected in certain areas in northern and northeastern regions," he said.
The ministry advised farmers to wait until August to avoid possible damage to plantings that may be caused by insufficient rains, the official said.
In June the agriculture ministry projected the 1997/98 first rice crop would top 18 million tonnes. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
